task: Choose the correct option: We ___ wait two hours at the airport last night.
explanation shown to learner: A past obligation: *had to*. *Must* has no past form.
explanation in Latvian: Pagātnes pienākums: *had to*. *Must* nav pagātnes formas.

task: Choose the correct option: I ___ finish the report before the meeting yesterday.
explanation shown to learner: A past obligation: *had to*. *Must* has no past form.
explanation in Latvian: Pagātnes pienākums: *had to*. *Must* nav pagātnes formas.

task: Choose the correct option: She ___ call the bank tomorrow morning.
explanation shown to learner: A future obligation: *will have to*. *Must* cannot follow *will*.
explanation in Latvian: Nākotnes pienākums: *will have to*. Aiz *will nevar* lietot *must*.

task: Correct the sentence. Keep *will*: We will can visit you next summer.
correct answer: We will be able to visit you next summer. | We'll be able to visit you next summer. | Next summer we will be able to visit you. | Next summer we'll be able to visit you.
explanation shown to learner: *Can* has no future form: *will be able to*.
explanation in Latvian: *Can* nav nākotnes formas: *will be able to*.

task: Remove one unnecessary word: I must to wear a uniform at work.
correct answer: I must wear a uniform at work.
explanation shown to learner: After *must* comes the base form, without *to*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *must* lieto darbības vārda pamatformu bez to.

task: I'm sorry, I ___ come to your party last Saturday. I was ill. (can)
explanation shown to learner: The past of *can* is *could*; the negative is *couldn't*.

task: When I was ten, I ___ swim really well. (can)
explanation shown to learner: An ability in the past: *could*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: you don't have to bring any food
explanation shown to learner: *don't have to* = it is not necessary.

task: Choose the correct option: The train is ___ than the bus.
explanation shown to learner: A short adjective + *-er* + *than*: *fast → faster*.

task: Choose the correct option: This is the ___ day of my holiday.
explanation shown to learner: *good → better → the best*: an irregular adjective.
explanation in Latvian: *good → better → the best*: neregulārs īpašības vārds.

task: My new phone is ___ than my old one. (cheap)
explanation shown to learner: A short adjective + *-er* + *than*: *fast → faster*.

task: My suitcase is ___ than yours. (heavy)
explanation shown to learner: *-y* changes to *-ier*: *heavy → heavier*.

task: My new flat is ___ than my old one. (big)
explanation shown to learner: One vowel + one consonant: double the consonant: *big → bigger*.
explanation in Latvian: Viens *patskanis* + viens līdzskanis: līdzskani dubulto: *big → bigger*.

task: Choose the correct option: Who is the ___ person in your family?
explanation shown to learner: *the* + adjective + *-est*: *the oldest*.

task: Correct the mistake: My sister is more young than me.
correct answer: My sister is younger than me. | My sister is younger than I am.
explanation shown to learner: A short adjective takes *-er*, not *more*.

task: Choose the correct option: My phone is the same ___ yours.
explanation shown to learner: *the same as*.

task: Choose the correct option: This film is not as good ___ the book.
explanation shown to learner: *not as ... as*.

task: The weather is getting ___ and ___. (cold)
explanation shown to learner: A change: comparative + *and* + comparative.

task: Write one word in each gap: Flights cost more every year. They are getting ___ and ___ expensive.
explanation shown to learner: A long adjective: *more and more expensive*.
explanation in Latvian: Garš īpašības vārds: *more and more expensive*.

task: Correct the mistake: This course is more easier than the last one.
correct answer: This course is easier than the last one.
explanation shown to learner: *-er* or *more*, never both.

task: Correct the mistake: My new job is more better than my old one.
correct answer: My new job is better than my old one.
explanation shown to learner: *better* is already a comparative: no *more*.

task: Choose the correct option: The ___ you practise, the better you get.
explanation shown to learner: *the more ..., the better ...*.

task: Choose the correct option: You ___ use your phone in the exam.
explanation shown to learner: A rule: *mustn't* + base form.

task: Choose the correct option: My son ___ ride a bike.
explanation shown to learner: *can* has no *-s* and no *to* after it.
explanation in Latvian: *can* nav *galotnes -s*, un aiz tā nav to.

task: Put all the words in order. More than one answer is possible.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: should we take an umbrella
explanation shown to learner: A statement has *we should take*; a question has *should we take*. Both fit the open instruction.
explanation in Latvian: Apgalvojumā ir *we should take*, jautājumā — *should we take*. Atvērtajai instrukcijai atbilst abi varianti.

task: Choose the correct option: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
explanation shown to learner: *should* + base form, no *to*.

task: Choose the correct option: ___ you help me with this box, please?
explanation shown to learner: A request: *Can you* + base form. *Can* has no *-s* and no *to*.
explanation in Latvian: Lūgums: *Can you* + pamatforma. *Can* nav *galotnes -s*, un aiz tā nav to.

task: Choose the correct option: I ___ drive. I don't have a licence.
explanation shown to learner: The negative of *can* is *can't*.

task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: *must not* + base form: it is not allowed.

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: She took the job despite the fact that the pay was low.
wrong options / checks: She took the job despite of the fact that the pay was low. | She took the job in spite the fact that the pay was low.
explanation shown to learner: *despite / in spite of* + noun or *-ing*; never *despite of*.
explanation in Latvian: *despite / in spite of* + lietvārds vai *-ing*; nekad *despite of*.

task: Choose the correct option: I left early so as ___ late.
explanation shown to learner: *so as not to* + base form.

task: Complete with one word: She spoke slowly so ___ to be understood.
explanation shown to learner: *so as to* + base form: purpose.

task: Correct the mistake: Despite of the delay, we arrived on time.
correct answer: Despite the delay, we arrived on time. | In spite of the delay, we arrived on time.
explanation shown to learner: *despite / in spite of* + noun or *-ing*; never *despite of*.
explanation in Latvian: *despite / in spite of* + lietvārds vai *-ing*; nekad *despite of*.

task: Complete with one word: In ___ of the cold, they went swimming.
explanation shown to learner: *despite / in spite of* + noun or *-ing*; never *despite of*.
explanation in Latvian: *despite / in spite of* + lietvārds vai *-ing*; nekad *despite of*.

task: Choose the correct option: ___ feeling ill, he went to work.
explanation shown to learner: *despite / in spite of* + noun or *-ing*; never *despite of*.
explanation in Latvian: *despite / in spite of* + lietvārds vai *-ing*; nekad *despite of*.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Which question is correct?
wrong options / checks: Who are you talking? | To who you are talking?
explanation shown to learner: In a question the preposition stays at the end: *Who are you talking to?*
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā prievārds paliek beigās: *Who are you talking to?* *Tulkojot burtiski* 'ar ko *tu* runā', prievārdu liek sākumā, bet angliski tas paliek beigās.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Complete with one word: What are you afraid ___?
explanation shown to learner: *afraid of*.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: In a question the preposition stays at the end: *Who are you talking to?*
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā prievārds paliek beigās: *Who are you talking to?* *Tulkojot burtiski* 'ar ko *tu* runā', prievārdu liek sākumā, bet angliski tas paliek beigās.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: *married to* someone; the preposition stays at the end. In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: *married to*; prievārds paliek beigās. Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Which team do you play ___?
explanation shown to learner: *play for* a team.

topic: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)
task: Choose the correct question.
wrong options / checks: What is about this book? | About what this book is?
explanation shown to learner: In a question the preposition stays at the end: *Who are you talking to?*
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā prievārds paliek beigās: *Who are you talking to?* *Tulkojot burtiski* 'ar ko *tu* runā', prievārdu liek sākumā, bet angliski tas paliek beigās.

task: Which is correct? 'If I ___ in your position, I'd ask for a pay rise.'
explanation shown to learner: *If I were you / in your position* + *would*.

task: If the city ___ more cycle lanes, more people ___ by bike. (build / travel)
explanation shown to learner: *if* + past, *would* + base form.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: If I would have a car, I would drive to work.
wrong options / checks: If she lived nearer, she'd visit more often. | We would travel more if flights were cheaper. | If he knew the answer, he would tell us all.
explanation shown to learner: No *would* after *if*: *If I had a car*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *if* nelieto *would*: *If I had a car.*

task: I don't have a car, so I take the bus. Imagine it is different. Choose the correct sentence.
correct answer: If I had a car, I wouldn't take the bus.
wrong options / checks: If I have a car, I wouldn't take the bus. | If I would have a car, I wouldn't take the bus. | If I had a car, I won't take the bus.
explanation shown to learner: An imagined present: *if* + past, *would* + base form.

task: Write the sentence with if: I don't have a garden, so I don't grow vegetables.
correct answer: If I had a garden, I would grow vegetables. | If I had a garden, I'd grow vegetables. | I would grow vegetables if I had a garden. | I'd grow vegetables if I had a garden.
explanation shown to learner: *if* + past, *would* + base form.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: We got lost yesterday because we didn't check the map. Imagine the opposite: 'If we ___ the map, we ___ lost.'
wrong options / checks: checked / wouldn't get | had checked / wouldn't get | would check / hadn't got
explanation shown to learner: *if* + *had* + 3rd form, *would have* + 3rd form.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: She stayed late and missed the last bus. If she ___ (not / stay) so late, she ___ (not / miss) the last bus.
explanation shown to learner: *if* + *had* + 3rd form, *would have* + 3rd form.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If they'd have asked me, I would've helped.
wrong options / checks: If it had rained, we'd have stayed in. | She would have come if you'd invited her. | If I had known, I wouldn't have said it.
explanation shown to learner: No *would have* after *if*: *If they had asked me*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *if* nelieto *would have*: *If they had asked me.*

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: We didn't know about the problem yesterday, so we didn't call you. Choose the sentence that says the opposite.
correct answer: If we had known about the problem, we would have called you.
wrong options / checks: If we had knew about the problem, we would have called you. | If we would have known about the problem, we would call you. | If we had known about the problem, we will have called you.
explanation shown to learner: *if* + *had* + 3rd form, *would have* + 3rd form.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Write the sentence with if: I didn't know about the sale, so I didn't buy the coat.
correct answer: If I had known about the sale, I would have bought the coat. | I would have bought the coat if I had known about the sale. | If I'd known about the sale, I'd have bought the coat. | If I'd known about the sale, I would have bought the coat. | If I had known about the sale, I'd have bought the coat. | I'd have bought the coat if I'd known about the sale. | I would have bought the coat if I'd known about the sale. | I'd have bought the coat if I had known about the sale.
explanation shown to learner: *if* + *had* + 3rd form, *would have* + 3rd form.

task: Choose the correct option: ___ for your help, we would never have finished on time.
explanation shown to learner: *But for* + noun = *If it hadn't been for*.
explanation in Latvian: *But for* + lietvārds = *If it hadn't been for.*

task: Rewrite starting with *Were*: If the price were lower, more people would buy it.
correct answer: Were the price lower, more people would buy it. | Were the price lower, more people would buy the product.
explanation shown to learner: *Were* + subject = *If* + subject + *were*, in formal English.

task: Choose the most formal option.
correct answer: Should you have questions, let us know.
wrong options / checks: If you've got questions, just shout. | Got any questions? Just let us know. | Any questions, just give us a call.
explanation shown to learner: *Should you ...* = *If you ...*, in formal writing.

task: ___ he ___ harder, he would have passed the exam.
explanation shown to learner: *Had he studied* = *If he had studied*: *had* before the subject, then the 3rd form.
explanation in Latvian: *Had he studied = If he had studied*: *had* pirms teikuma priekšmeta, tad 3. forma.

task: ___ it not been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.
explanation shown to learner: *Had it not been for* = *If it hadn't been for*.
explanation in Latvian: *Had it not been for = If it hadn't been for.*

topic: Unreal time and preferences (it's high time, I'd rather)
task: Choose the correct option: It's high time we ___ a decision.
explanation shown to learner: *It's (high) time* + subject + past: something should already be happening.
explanation in Latvian: *It's* (*high*) *time* + teikuma priekšmets + pagātne: tam jau būtu jānotiek.

topic: Unreal time and preferences (it's high time, I'd rather)
task: I'd rather you ___ anyone about this yet.
wrong options / checks: bank: didn't tell | don't tell | won't tell | not to tell
explanation shown to learner: *I'd rather* + another person + past: what we want someone else to do.
explanation in Latvian: *I'd rather* + cits cilvēks + pagātne: ko *gribam*, lai dara kāds cits.

task: I was in hospital, so I missed your wedding. Choose the correct sentence.
correct answer: I wish I could have come to your wedding.
wrong options / checks: I wish I could come to your wedding. | I wish I can have come to your wedding. | I wish I would come to your wedding.
explanation shown to learner: A past ability we regret: *wish* + *could have* + 3rd form.
explanation in Latvian: Nožēla par pagātnē neiespējamo: *wish + could have* + 3. forma.

task: You talk about a past mistake in a meeting. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If only we had tested the app, we would not have these problems.
wrong options / checks: If only we would have tested the app, we would not have these problems. | If only we tested the app, we would not have these problems. | If only we had tested the app, we will not have these problems.
explanation shown to learner: *If only* + past perfect for the past; *would* for the result now.
explanation in Latvian: *If only* + Past Perfect par pagātni; *would* par sekām tagad.

topic: Unreal time and preferences (it's high time, I'd rather)
task: Write one sentence that starts with *I'd rather*: Please don't call me after ten.
correct answer: I'd rather you didn't call me after ten. | I would rather you didn't call me after ten. | I'd rather you didn't call me after ten o'clock. | I would rather you didn't call me after ten o'clock. | I'd rather you not call me after ten. | I would rather you not call me after ten.
explanation shown to learner: *I'd rather* + another person + past.

task: Which sentence reports 'You lost my keys!' as an accusation?
correct answer: He accused me of losing his keys.
wrong options / checks: He accused me to lose his keys. | He accused me that I lost his keys. | He accused me for losing his keys.
explanation shown to learner: *accuse* someone *of* + -ing.

task: Report with *advise*: 'Don't sign anything until you've read it,' the lawyer told her.
correct answer: The lawyer advised her not to sign anything until she had read it. | The lawyer advised her not to sign anything until she'd read it. | The lawyer advised her not to sign anything until she read it.
explanation shown to learner: *advise* someone *not to* + verb; *you've read* becomes *she had read*.
explanation in Latvian: *advise* kādu *not to* + darbības vārds; *you've read* kļūst par *she had read*.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She insisted to pay for dinner.
wrong options / checks: She offered to pay for the tickets. | He admitted taking the money. | They suggested going by train.
explanation shown to learner: *insist on* + -ing: *She insisted on paying*.

task: Which sentence reports this: 'We're sorry the train was late, and we'll give you a refund.'
correct answer: The company apologised for the delay and promised a refund.
wrong options / checks: The company apologised the delay and promised a refund. | The company apologised for the delay and promised refunding. | The company apologised for the delay and promised of a refund.
explanation shown to learner: *apologise for* something; *promise* + noun or *to* + verb.
explanation in Latvian: *apologise for; promise* + lietvārds vai to + darbības vārds.

task: Report with *deny*: 'It wasn't me who sent that email to the whole company,' said Leo.
correct answer: Leo denied sending that email to the whole company. | Leo denied having sent that email to the whole company. | Leo denied that he had sent that email to the whole company. | Leo denied he had sent that email to the whole company. | Leo denied that he sent that email to the whole company. | Leo denied he sent that email to the whole company. | Leo denied sending the email to the whole company. | Leo denied having sent the email to the whole company.
explanation shown to learner: *deny* + -ing (or *having* + 3rd form).

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Which sentence is correct and polite?
correct answer: Would you mind telling me where the nearest pharmacy is?
wrong options / checks: Would you mind telling me where is the nearest pharmacy? | Would you mind to tell me where the nearest pharmacy is? | Would you mind telling me where the nearest pharmacy is it?
explanation shown to learner: After *Could you tell me / Do you know* the word order is like a statement: subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *Could you tell me / Do you know* vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Ask politely, starting with *Could you tell me*: Why is the flight delayed?
correct answer: Could you tell me why the flight is delayed? | Could you tell me why the flight's delayed?
explanation shown to learner: After *Could you tell me / Do you know* the word order is like a statement: subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *Could you tell me / Do you know* vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: Do you know what time does it open?
wrong options / checks: Do you know if Anna is at home? | I wonder how far the station is. | Could you tell me who called me?
explanation shown to learner: After *Could you tell me / Do you know* the word order is like a statement: subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *Could you tell me / Do you know* vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Which is the polite way to ask this: 'Where is the meeting room?'
correct answer: I was wondering if you could tell me where the meeting room is.
wrong options / checks: I was wondering if you could tell me where is the meeting room. | I was wondering if could you tell me where the meeting room is. | I was wondering you could tell me where the meeting room is.
explanation shown to learner: After *Could you tell me / Do you know* the word order is like a statement: subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *Could you tell me / Do you know* vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Ask politely, starting with *Do you know*: When does the shop close?
correct answer: Do you know when the shop closes?
explanation shown to learner: After *Could you tell me / Do you know* the word order is like a statement: subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *Could you tell me / Do you know* vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds.

task: Choose the correct option: I can't concentrate. There are ___ people here.
explanation shown to learner: *too many* + plural nouns; *too much* + uncountable nouns.

task: Choose the correct option: We can't make a cake. There isn't ___ flour.
explanation shown to learner: *enough* + noun, without *of*.

task: Write the missing word: Is your car big ___ for five people?
explanation shown to learner: adjective + *enough*: *big enough*.

task: Choose the correct option: There was ___ much traffic, so we were late.
explanation shown to learner: *too much* = more than is good.

task: Choose the correct option: I've got ___ money, so I can't come to the cinema.
explanation shown to learner: *little* + uncountable nouns (*money*); *few* + plurals.
